forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Bradford Council's 2025-26 accounts: £113m overspend, usable reserves up £55m to £229.2m, clean audit opinion expected
news_drafts.lead:
Bradford Council ended 2025-26 with usable reserves of £229.2m, up £55.0m on the year, even though its day-to-day spending ran £113m over budget, the Governance and Audit Committee heard on 24 September. The council's statement of accounts, its formal annual accounts, says the overspend was £14m smaller than first forecast and was paid for through a capitalisation direction, government permission to treat day-to-day spending as capital spending so it can be funded by borrowing or asset sales. The accounts say part of the rise in reserves comes from earmarking costs funded that way. The general fund balance, the cushion for the unexpected, is £53.1m, or 3.5% of about £1.5bn of gross spending.

The council's external auditor, Forvis Mazars, anticipates an unqualified opinion, meaning a full sign-off, on the accounts. That is subject to remaining work, including investment property valuations, land and buildings indexation, pension liability work, capital grants and long-term borrowing balances. The council says no material changes were needed to its primary statements and that it has no audit backlog. Overall materiality, the level of error the auditor treats as significant, is £31.5m.

The accounts record a £23.7m net fall from revaluing buildings, park land and investment properties. Non-current assets fell £13.2m overall despite £79.4m of capital enhancements. The Executive's July 2026 decision not to proceed with the Square Lane project means £4.9m of abortive costs will be charged to day-to-day spending, taking usable reserves from £229.2m to £224.3m.

The council's pension scheme has assets of £3.1bn against liabilities of £2.2bn, a surplus of £871m. An accounting restriction known as the asset ceiling means no net pension asset appears on the balance sheet.

Separately, the West Yorkshire Pension Fund's audit report anticipates an unqualified opinion. Its auditor found a £60.9m understatement in hard-to-value investments, which management corrected, and left £30.3m of estimated further error unadjusted. A revised transaction report raised recorded purchases and sales by £842.4m after testing found the first did not match supporting evidence.

findings.paper_title: Doc Q - COBMDC - Internal Audit Strategy and 2026-27 Annual Plan - FINAL post CMT
findings.headline: £46 million annual highways grant income requires compliance audit verification
findings.detail: The Highways Department received £46 million in grant income in 2025-26 and a 30-day priority audit is planned to verify compliance with grant conditions. This indicates material grant dependency and recognition of clawback risk.
findings.matters: Significant grant dependency creates clawback and cash flow risk if compliance fails; audit focus indicates the council treats this as a control priority.
findings.figures: £46 million grant income to Highways in 2025-26
findings.quote: the Highways Department received £46million in grant income in 2025-26. We will audit the Department's arrangements for compliance with grant conditions.

findings.paper_title: Doc Q - COBMDC - Internal Audit Strategy and 2026-27 Annual Plan - FINAL post CMT
findings.headline: Workforce cost control audits planned for agency workers, overtime, and sickness absence
findings.detail: Workforce identified as a strategic risk category. Priority audits allocate 30 days to agency worker management and 30 days to overtime payment controls; an indicative 40-day audit of sickness absence management is also planned, indicating management concern about labor cost control.
findings.matters: Labor costs are typically material to council budgets; multiple focused audits on agency workers and overtime suggest management concern about cost control or compliance in discretionary spend areas.
findings.figures: Agency workers audit: 30 days; Overtime: 30 days; Sickness absence audit (indicative): 40 days
findings.quote: Use of Agency Workers- we will audit the Council's arrangements for the management and payment of agency worker staff.

findings.paper_title: Doc Q - COBMDC - Internal Audit Strategy and 2026-27 Annual Plan - FINAL post CMT
findings.headline: Financial Resilience & Sustainability established as a primary strategic risk driving audit planning
findings.detail: The council's August 2026 risk assessment identifies Financial Resilience & Sustainability as one of 14 strategic risk categories. Multiple priority audits are mapped to this risk category including cash and treasury management, property and asset management, scheme of delegation, and agency worker controls.
findings.matters: The council's own risk assessment identifies financial sustainability as requiring targeted audit and management attention; this signals to a lender how the council rates its own financial resilience.
findings.figures: Financial Resilience & Sustainability one of 14 strategic risks; 7 priority audits mapped to this risk category
findings.quote: The Council's risk profile as at August 2026 included 14 risk categories as outlined below:

findings.paper_title: Doc Q - COBMDC - Internal Audit Strategy and 2026-27 Annual Plan - FINAL post CMT
findings.headline: Bradford Children's & Families Trust identified as strategic sustainability risk but excluded from audit scope
findings.detail: Internal audit explicitly provides assurance to the council and WYPF only, with BCFT and other subsidiaries not audited. Yet BCFT is listed as one of 14 strategic risk categories (BCFT – Sustainability), creating a governance gap where a subsidiary carrying identified sustainability risk lacks independent assurance oversight.
findings.matters: A subsidiary carrying a named sustainability risk operates without internal audit oversight, limiting visibility of control effectiveness or financial distress indicators.
findings.figures: BCFT identified as one of 14 strategic risks; audit coverage explicitly excludes it and other subsidiaries
findings.quote: IA currently provides audit services to the Council and WYPF but not to BCFT or other subsidiaries.

findings.paper_title: Doc Q - COBMDC - Internal Audit Strategy and 2026-27 Annual Plan - FINAL post CMT
findings.headline: Audit function carrying 5 vacancies with only 30 days contingency, limiting governance assurance delivery
findings.detail: The internal audit team has 5 unfilled vacancies acting as a limiting factor on audit volume. Resource availability (650 days) barely exceeds requirement (620 days), leaving only 30 days contingency to respond to emerging risks or priority changes. All planned audits target completion by end April 2027.
findings.matters: Governance and control oversight depend on adequate assurance capacity; constrained audit resources limit the council's ability to identify and remediate control weaknesses or emerging risks.
findings.figures: 5 vacancies; 620 days required; 650 days available; 30 days contingency
findings.quote: The audit team is currently carrying 5 vacancies which acts as a limiting factor on the volume of audits which can be delivered.
